definition: TIMIT is a corpus of phonemically and lexically transcribed speech of American English speakers of different sexes and dialects.
details: Each transcribed element has been delineated in time. TIMIT was designed to further acoustic-phonetic knowledge and automatic speech recognition systems. It was commissioned by DARPA and corpus design was a joint effort between the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, SRI International, and Texas Instruments (TI). The speech was recorded at TI, transcribed at MIT, and verified and prepared for publishing by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). There is also a telephone bandwidth version called NTIMIT (Network TIMIT). TIMIT and NTIMIT are not freely available — either membership of the Linguistic Data Consortium, or a monetary payment, is required for access to the dataset.

explainer.lead: TIMIT is a corpus of phonemically and lexically transcribed American English speech from speakers of different sexes and dialects. It matters as a foundational resource for acoustic-phonetic research and automatic speech recognition.

tiers.eli5: A carefully labelled collection of recorded voices, marked up sound by sound, used to teach computers to understand speech.
tiers.practitioner: Commonly used to train and benchmark speech recognition systems and phone-level models. Pitfall: it is small and not representative of all real-world audio, so results may not generalize.
tiers.paperLevel: A speech corpus in which each transcribed element is delineated in time; commissioned by DARPA, designed jointly by MIT, SRI International, and Texas Instruments, recorded at TI, transcribed at MIT, and verified and prepared by NIST.

explainer.example: Each phoneme and word in a recorded sentence carries start and end timestamps, letting a model learn alignment between audio and text.
